title: U.S. House · Oklahoma's 2nd District
area: Eastern Oklahoma, including Muskogee, McAlester and the Cherokee, Choctaw and Muscogee reservation areas

candidates.name: Josh Brecheen

summary.text: Josh Brecheen is the Republican incumbent for Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2023. A rancher and former excavation and trucking business owner, he served in the Oklahoma State Senate from 2010 to 2018. According to his official biography, he is focused on reducing federal debt and deficit spending.

background.text: Born in Pontotoc County, Oklahoma; graduated from Coalgate High School. His official biography describes him as a fourth-generation rancher from eastern Oklahoma.
Earned a dual degree in agriculture from Oklahoma State University and served as state president of the Oklahoma FFA Association from 1998 to 1999.
Ran a motivational speaking business, Brecheen Keynotes and Seminars, until 2010, and has raised performance horses for over 20 years, according to his official biography.
Worked for six years for U.S. Senator Tom Coburn as a field representative, and later owned and operated a small excavation and trucking business.
Elected to the Oklahoma State Senate in 2010, defeating Democratic incumbent Jay Paul Gumm; he served District 6 until 2018, when he did not file for re-election.

Won the August 23, 2022 Republican primary runoff for the open 2nd District seat over Avery Frix (52.2% to 47.8%), then the November general election with 72.4% of the vote, succeeding Markwayne Mullin.
Re-elected in 2024 with 74.2% over Democrat Brandon Wade and independent Ronnie Hopkins, and won the June 16, 2026 Republican primary with 79.2% over William Webb.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Budget Committee and the House Homeland Security Committee, where he is a member of the Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee and chairman of the Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability Subcommittee.
Lives in eastern Oklahoma; his official biography describes him as a Christian, husband and father.

priorities.text: Lists deficit spending, border security, traditional values, constitutional adherence and energy dominance as his legislative priorities.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately. His official site lists legislative priority categories (deficit spending, border security, traditional values, constitutional adherence, energy dominance) without accompanying position statements or press releases explaining each in detail; only border security could be tied to a specific documented action (current committee assignment).

candidates.name: Brandon Wade

summary.text: Brandon Wade is the Democratic nominee for Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District and a rural Oklahoman from Washington County. He works in the oil industry and is a union committee chairman and executive board officer with IUOE Local 351. He was also the party's nominee in 2024, and describes his campaign as focused on bipartisan representation and protecting reproductive rights.

background.text: Born in Bartlesville, Oklahoma, and raised in rural Copan, where he graduated from Copan High School, according to his survey.
Describes himself as a third-generation working-class union member who has held his job for almost 23 years.
Career experience as a laborer in the oil industry; has served as union committee chairman and as an executive board member (Vice President) for IUOE Local 351.
Was the Democratic nominee for the 2nd District in 2024, receiving 21.4% against incumbent Josh Brecheen.
Won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary with 73.7% of the vote over Erik Terwey.

priorities.text: "Returning Real Representation to our Congress" by listening to voters of all parties rather than following party lines.
priorities.quote: Returning Real Representation to our Congress. To do this we must listen to all voters, from all parties.

positions.summary: Says he is passionate about restoring women's rights to make their own healthcare decisions.
positions.quote: Restoring our women’s rights. We must make sure that our women have the right to privacy in their healthcare and our able to make their own decisions about their health and bodies.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Ronnie Hopkins

summary.text: Ronnie Hopkins is an independent candidate for Oklahoma's 2nd Congressional District and also ran in the 2024 race for the seat. Little biographical information about him is published; his 2024 campaign website listed support for the Constitution, biblical principles and cutting foreign aid.

background.text: Ran as an independent in the November 5, 2024 general election for the 2nd District, receiving 4.4% of the vote (14,061 votes) behind Josh Brecheen and Brandon Wade.

His 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, described a platform that includes support for "biblical principles," the U.S. Constitution, turning Social Security into a "real trust fund," and veterans and gun rights.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia's page for Ronnie Hopkins lists his 2024 and 2026 candidacies but no biographical section, and he has not completed a Candidate Connection survey; his birthplace, education and occupation could not be found.
